title: Stable-id assignment uses two refs plus a dependency-less effect performing a render-phase state write-back
description: Stable row keys are produced by: (a) calling `ensureRuleIds(rawRules)` on every render, (b) a `prevRulesRef`/`didAssignIds` ref pair plus a `[rawRules]` effect to reset a guard, and (c) a second effect with intentionally no deps that runs after every render to fire `onUpdateFactor({ rules })`. This is a side-effecting write-back of persisted state purely to obtain React keys, and its correctness depends on the parent round-tripping `_id` unchanged and not memo-stripping it. The whole mechanism can be replaced by deriving keys without persisting them — e.g. a module-level `WeakMap<rule, string>` assigned lazily inside `ruleKey`, or `useMemo` mapping rule identity to ids — which removes both refs, both effects, the eslint-disable on the no-dep effect, and the parent write-back entirely. That also resolves finding #1 (no `_id` ever enters the wire model).
evidence: Lines 201-216: `didAssignIds`/`prevRulesRef` + `useEffect(...,[rawRules])` reset + `useEffect(() => { if (rules !== rawRules && !didAssignIds.current) { ...; onUpdateFactor({ rules }) } })` with comment '// intentionally no deps — runs on every render'. `ruleKey` (line 33-35) already falls back to `fallback_${index}` so keys never hard-depend on persisted `_id`.
est_reduction: ~15-20 lines (remove ensureRuleIds persistence, two refs, two effects, one eslint-disable)
behavior_preservation: Row keys remain stable across edits/reorders via object-identity map; deletion/insert behavior and all existing tests on _id presence would need updating since _id would no longer be emitted to onUpdateFactor (behavioral change limited to the synthetic key, not rule data).
